landmarks.name: Renaissance Center
landmarks.summary: Henry Ford II's cluster of mirrored glass towers on the river, built to save downtown and walled off from it. The central Westin is the tallest hotel in the Western Hemisphere.

landmarks.name: Tiger Stadium
landmarks.summary: The double-decked ballpark at Michigan and Trumbull where the Tigers won it all in 1984. The upper deck in right field hangs out over the field.

landmarks.name: Joe Louis Arena
landmarks.summary: The Red Wings' concrete riverfront arena, where fans throw octopuses onto the ice in the playoffs. Its giant fist sculpture honours the Brown Bomber nearby.

landmarks.name: Cobo Hall
landmarks.summary: The convention hall on the river where the auto show unveils the new models each January. Martin Luther King Jr. first gave a version of his Dream speech here in 1963.

landmarks.name: Fox Theatre
landmarks.summary: The 1928 'Siamese Byzantine' movie palace on Woodward, the second largest in the country, grimy and fading. Rumour says someone with deep pockets is about to restore it.

landmarks.name: Fisher Building
landmarks.summary: The Fisher brothers' Art Deco tower in New Center, its three-storey arcade gilded and painted like a cathedral. The finest building in a city of fine buildings.

landmarks.name: Guardian Building
landmarks.summary: The orange-brick Art Deco 'Cathedral of Finance' downtown, its banking hall a riot of Pewabic tile and Aztec patterns. Bankers still work under its painted vaults.

landmarks.name: Hitsville U.S.A.
landmarks.summary: The little house on West Grand Boulevard where Berry Gordy made Motown, with Studio A in the basement. Motown left for Los Angeles in 1972; the museum opened last year.

landmarks.name: Detroit Institute of Arts
landmarks.summary: The Beaux-Arts museum on Woodward whose courtyard is wrapped in Diego Rivera's Detroit Industry murals. The city's crown jewel, through every hard time.

landmarks.name: Belle Isle
landmarks.summary: Olmsted's island park in the Detroit River, with its aquarium, conservatory and the Scott Fountain. Teenagers cruise its loop road on summer nights.

landmarks.name: Michigan Central Station
landmarks.summary: The towering Beaux-Arts station in Corktown, its office tower empty and only a few Amtrak trains a day left. Rumours say even those will soon stop.

landmarks.name: Eastern Market
landmarks.summary: The open-air market sheds where farmers, butchers and flower sellers fill the streets every Saturday. The oldest public market in the country.

landmarks.name: Greektown
landmarks.summary: Monroe Street's Greek restaurants and bakeries, where waiters set saganaki alight with a cry of 'Opa!'. Bustling late into the night while downtown empties.

landmarks.name: Penobscot Building
landmarks.summary: The 47-storey Art Deco tower of 1928, long the tallest in the city, with a red light on its mast. Its lobby is decorated with Native American motifs.

landmarks.name: Hudson's
landmarks.summary: The giant J. L. Hudson department store on Woodward, the second largest store in the world, closed since 1983 and standing empty. Its famous Christmas floor is only a memory.

landmarks.name: Ambassador Bridge
landmarks.summary: The suspension bridge to Windsor, Canada, the busiest border crossing in North America. Owned, unusually, by a private businessman.

landmarks.name: Henry Ford Museum
landmarks.summary: Ford's vast museum of American invention in Dearborn, with the bus Rosa Parks rode and the chair Lincoln was shot in. Greenfield Village next door has Edison's lab.

landmarks.name: Ford Rouge Plant
landmarks.summary: The mile-long Rouge plant in Dearborn, where iron ore went in one end and Model A's came out the other. The UAW's Battle of the Overpass was fought at its gate in 1937.

1980s.transitNote: No rail transit: the People Mover opened in 1987, the QLine in 2017.
